pr_comments:
Hey there @fabaff, mind taking a look at this pull request as it has been labeled with an integration (`scrape`) you are listed as a [code owner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L449) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

It does not appear that there are any existing unit tests for the `scrape` integration.  I've never developed unit tests before, and to create one from scratch for a HA core integration is a bit beyond my experience and comfort level.

Given the the nature of the change - simply leveraging `get` to gracefully retrieve a dictionary value without an exception - can this be merged without standing up new unit test suite from scratch?  I think it would be better to see that established through a separate PR .

@MizterB So is the falling function always able to handle the `None` condition and is it appropriate in all these cases where the key `self._attr` does not exist to silently return `None` without any error or warning?

I don't use the scrape integration but it feels like this could mask a problem (& make debugging harder) if the content being scraped ever changed.

The proposed code does not change the sensor behavior - if an attribute has a value assigned to it, it will continue to return that value.  

The current code can never return a None value, so introducing that result should not break existing sensors.

At the same time, the current approach of raising an exception and failing to create the sensor at all is problematic.  It is a one-time check against a potentially dynamic value.  If you consider the example provided in https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/58245, the sensor would fail to be created at all if a checkbox happened to be unselected at the time that HA starts.  

But it would be created if the box happened to checked at HA startup.  If it later becomes unchecked, exceptions are thrown in the log, but the value of the sensor fails to update.  It retains the previous state, and does not reflect an error condition.  

Given the above, I feel like relying on exceptions is inappropriate for this use case, and the proposed change of providing a result that cannot be returned in the current code is low risk.

My comment was more related to the fact that web scraping is inherently unpredictable and does not handle web server changes well.  

I don't mean that existing sensors would break with this PR.

But if the web page changed in the future and a key got deleted, what would be the indication to the user that something was wrong?  Could this PR mask it?

Is there any way that if the integration can't scrape a key that it was expecting it can tell someone (eg warning log maybe?)

OK, I understand the feedback now.  To better informing the user, if the attribute or index values don't exist, the exceptions are captured are logged as warnings.  In those cases, I return resulting value as None, which allow the user the ability to handle that condition in the value_template, if desired.

I have some linting errors to take care, but would appreciate your feedback on the general approach.
Looks good to me! Thanks for adding the warnings!

issue_context.title: Scrape sensor cannot parse attributes that are not key/value pairs
issue_context.body:
### The problem

The scrape sensor is unable to parse HTML input attributes that are not key/value pairs.  

For example, a checkbox input can be defined as follows:

Selected -> `<input type="CHECKBOX" name="PRIVACY" value="on" checked>`
Deselected -> `<input type="CHECKBOX" name="PRIVACY" value="on">`

However, the scraper throws an error when looking for the `checked` attribute if it is not present.  Therefore it cannot determine if a checkbox is actually "checked".

For example, scraping the above input tag with the following config:
```
select: "input[name='PRIVACY']"
attribute: checked
```
results in an error if the box is unchecked, because the `checked` attribute is not present.

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<string>", line 1, in <module>
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.9/site-packages/bs4/element.py", line 1486, in __getitem__
    return self.attrs[key]
KeyError: 'checked'
```

The scrape sensor should be modified to return `None` if an attribute cannot be found.  With this logic, the checkbox state can be correctly determined by a template:
```
value_template: >-
  {% if value == '' %}
  on
  {% elif value == none %}
  off
  {% endif %}
```

### What is version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2021.10.6

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

scrape

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/scrape/

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
See above
```


### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
See above
```
